This is a metered RydeTAXI trip: the rider was charged $34.83 with distance $22.50 over 15.96 km and time $6.96 over 26.8 min, base $3.90, platform $1.47, waiting $0.00, no surge [F4][F5][F6]. So the fixed-quote branch of RD-2 does not apply; extra kilometres enter the fare and the metered branch governs quantum [RD-2].

The GPS record establishes a longer trip than the optimal route — 16.0 km against 10.6 km (+5.4 km, +50%) in 26.8 min against 16.5 min estimated [F1][F2] — and one measured off-route segment, 09:13–09:24, driving 6.58 km where the optimal route covers 1.57 km, adding 5.01 km and reaching up to 1578 m off the optimal route [F3]. Under RD-1 that segment is an unexempted deviation unless RD-3, RD-4 or RD-5 excuses it; RD-1 sets no percentage or kilometre threshold [RD-1].

RD-4 cannot excuse it: the trace settles that there is no qualifying incident on the replaced stretch reported before the detour (✗), and F12 records no traffic incidents near the route during the trip window [F12][RD-4]. The only corridor records are speed bands — AYE band 2 (10–19 km/h) during 08:49–09:13, CTE band 5 (40–49 km/h) during 08:49–09:34, Kent Ridge Road band 3 during 08:49–09:34 [F9][F10][F11]. Under RD-4(b) a band record is corroboration only and does not exempt a segment on its own in this MVP; here the band window ends at 09:13, exactly when the segment begins, so it does not even cover the segment [F9][F3][RD-4]. Heavy rain of 18.5 mm [F13] explains slowness but is not a qualifying RD-4 record, and the driver's own statement that the AYE was crawling and flooding rests solely on a post-trip claim [F8][RD-4].

RD-5 likewise gives no consent: there are no in-app chat messages at all [F7], so there is no rider message agreeing to any route change before 09:13, and the driver's post-trip explanation [F8] is a claim, not rider consent [F7][F8][RD-5]. RD-3 does not apply — no rider-requested stop is measured in the segment, and the rider named no place [F3][F7][RD-3].

The segment therefore counts under RD-2. Amount: the trip's per-km rate is the distance fare ÷ distance km, $22.50 ÷ 15.96 = $1.4097...; the fare record states $7.53 ÷ 5.34 km = $1.4098/km [F4][F6]. Applying that rate to the unexempted segment's extra 5.01 km [F3]: 5.01 × $1.4098 = $7.0631 → $7.06 [F3][F4][RD-2]. The residual difference between the billed excess of 5.34 km ($7.53) [F4] and the segment's 5.01 km [F3] is mileage not attributed to any segment, which RD-2 expressly does not refund [RD-2].

RD-6's flag condition is not met: the case is made out under RD-2, but the trace settles route_disputes_upheld_90d = 0 and F15 shows the driver's route-dispute upheld count is 0, so this is not a "repeated" breach and no account flag is added [F15][RD-6].

rejected_claims.reason: The AYE band-2 record runs 08:49–09:13, ending the minute the off-route segment begins at 09:13 [F9][F3]; a band is corroboration only and does not exempt a segment on its own, and no incident on the replaced stretch exists [F12][RD-4].

Heavy rain of 18.5 mm [F13] explains a slow road but is not a qualifying RD-4 record; RD-4 requires traffic corroboration targeting the replaced portion of the optimal route, and F12 records no incident during the trip window [F12][RD-4].

The driver's statement says he 'went round' the expressway but names no road, and no fact ties the driven segment to the CTE [F8][F10]; the RD-4 exemption must target the replaced portion of the optimal route, not a different road's speed [RD-4].

The absence of chat cuts against the driver: RD-5 excuses a segment only on the rider's own prior message agreeing to it, and there is none [F7]; the driver's RD-1 duty to take the shortest and most direct route is independent of any rider instruction [F7][F8][RD-5].
The concession that only congestion is relied on still fails: the incident branch is settled unmet (no qualifying incident) [F12], and RD-4(b) does not exempt on a band record alone [F9][RD-4].

The segment's added distance is 5.01 km, but the rate is this trip's distance fare ÷ distance km as the fare record states it ($7.53 ÷ 5.34 km = $1.4098/km) [F4][F6]; 5.01 × $1.4098 = $7.06, not a rate recomputed from an unrounded figure [F3][F4][RD-2].
RD-6 requires an upheld route-dispute history (route_disputes_upheld_90d ≥ 1) for a flag; F15 shows the driver's route-dispute upheld count is 0, so no flag_account attaches [F15][RD-6].
Accepted in substance: the reachable figure is the segment's own extra km ($7.06), not the wider billed residual of $7.53, because RD-2 refuses mileage not attributed to any segment [F3][F4][RD-2].

segment_findings.reason: No in-app chat exists, so no rider message agrees to the route change before the segment started at 09:13 [F7]; the driver's post-trip explanation that the AYE was crawling and flooding is a claim in his own statement, not rider consent [F8]. RD-5 therefore excuses nothing, and RD-3 does not apply because no rider-requested, rider-named stop is recorded [F7]. RD-4 is settled as unmet (no qualifying incident on the replaced stretch) [F12], and a speed band alone does not exempt a segment, with the AYE band-2 window ending as the segment begins [F9]. The segment's 5.01 extra km is refundable under RD-2 [F3][F4].

Three kinds of agreement: (1) GENERAL route choice ('take whichever way is faster') covers a route chosen to get there, not an errand of the driver's own (a stop away from the route, a loop that reaches nothing: counts). (2) A SPECIFIC named road or area ('go round via X') covers driving on X only: the record must tie this segment to X (a stop on X, a message placing the car on X, a road name in a fact); timing alone does not, and the fact table carries no road names for the driven path — if nothing ties them, the finding is undetermined (G13); if the record places this segment somewhere else (a stop away from X, the driver's own statement naming another road or place, a stop the driver chose the location of), the agreement to X does not cover it: counts. (3) Scope unclear: undetermined. A driver's claim of agreement that appears only in his statement is not consent (G11); a complete chat record with no rider agreement before the segment: counts. This finding changes the amount. Any driver would have done the same.” (F8)

claims.assertion: This was a RydeTAXI metered trip (charged $34.83 with distance $22.50 for 15.96 km and time $6.96 for 26.8 min, base $3.90, platform $1.47, no waiting fee, F6), so unlike a fixed-quote Ryde service the extra kilometres drove the fare up and are refundable under the metered branch of RD-2.

The GPS record shows the driver covered 16.0 km against an optimal route of 10.6 km (+5.4 km, +50%) in 26.8 min against an estimated 16.5 min, so the shortest and most direct route obligation in RD-1 was breached in fact, not merely in the rider's impression.

One off-route segment is recorded, 09:13–09:24, in which 6.58 km was driven where the optimal route covers 1.57 km, adding 5.01 km and reaching up to 1578 m from the optimal route; this is an unexempted off-route segment because no exemption in RD-3, RD-4 or RD-5 applies to it (F7, F8, F12).

The driver never asked the rider: there are no in-app chat messages at all between rider and driver (F7), so there is no rider message agreeing to any route before the segment started at 09:13, and the driver's own statement that 'any driver would have done the same' (F8) was written after the trip and cannot be consent.

The driver's justification is a claim of congestion and flooding on the Ayer Rajah Expressway, but RD-4 requires a traffic incident fact on the replaced optimal route; the facts record no traffic incidents near the route during the trip window (F12), so the 'reasonable cause' exemption cannot be made out on the incident branch.

The only supporting traffic data are speed bands on the optimal-route corridors — Ayer Rajah Expressway band 2 (10–19 km/h) 08:49–09:13 (F9), Central Expressway band 5 (40–49 km/h) 08:49–09:34 (F10) and Kent Ridge Road band 3 (20–29 km/h) 08:49–09:34 (F11) — and under RD-4(b) a band record alone is corroboration only and does not exempt the segment in this MVP, all the more so when the segment ran 09:13–09:24, past the AYE band window (F3).

Because the segment is unexempted, RD-2 entitles the rider to a partial refund of the excess distance on a metered trip, computed as 5.01 km × the trip's per-km rate of $1.4098/km = $7.06, the per-km rate being taken from fare fact F4 ($7.53 ÷ 5.34 km) and the segment's added 5.01 km from F3.

The number the rider should expect is the unexempted segment's own added distance only: the billed excess of $7.53 over 5.34 km (F4) is slightly larger than the 5.01 km segment (F3), and RD-2 expressly refuses the residual mileage difference outside the segment, so $7.06 rather than $7.53 is the correct figure.

The driver's 90-day record shows 3 disputes with 2 upheld (F15), so if the judge adds any account action it should be a flag_account accompanying the refund, and that profile fact is offered only as support for the additional action, not as proof of this deviation.

The rider's own account (F14) shows a long-standing account with a 4.8 rating and no upheld disputes, and no threat, intimidation, harassment or dangerous-driving allegation appears in the complaint or in the driver's statement (F7, F8), so the case is fit for an ordinary fare determination rather than escalation.

weaknesses: Heavy rain is a recorded fact (F13) and the driver points to flooding (F8); a judge may treat the weather plus the AYE band-2 record (F9, 10–19 km/h, though it ends at 09:13 while the segment runs 09:13–09:24) as corroborating a genuine congestion reason, even though RD-4(b) says a band alone does not exempt a segment.

The billed excess in F4 is 5.34 km while the recorded segment in F3 adds only 5.01 km; the driver may argue the rider's own numbers show the complained-of detour is smaller than disputed, and RD-2 excludes the unsegmented residual, so the recoverable amount is modest.

There is no chat at all (F7), which cuts both ways: it defeats any consent argument, but it also means we have no contemporaneous rider message objecting during the 09:13–09:24 segment, and the driver may characterise the silence as acquiescence.

The driver's statement about the AYE (F8) is a post-trip claim with no road-name record tying the driven segment to any particular road; if the judge instead treats the driver's reason as a routing request issue the segment may be held undetermined (G13) and routed to manual review rather than refunded.
The rider's profile shows 1 dispute in 90 days with 0 upheld (F14), which the other side may cite as a history of unsuccessful complaints, though it is not probative of this deviation.

claims.assertion: The single off-route segment ran 09:13–09:24, and the GPS record shows that during the first 34 minutes of the trip window the Ayer Rajah Expressway — the expressway the driver says he avoided — was itself logged at speed band 2 (10–19 km/h), i.e. severe congestion on a road carrying traffic at walking pace on the optimal corridor (F9, F1).

The heavy rain recorded for the trip (18.5 mm, thundery showers) is the objective corroboration the driver's reroute explanation points to, and it matches his statement that he routed around the expressway because it was crawling and flooding (F13, F8).

No separate alternative route is needed to explain the detour as a safety/efficiency choice: the alternative expressway in the corridor (Central Expressway) was moving at speed band 5 (40–49 km/h) over the whole trip window, so a driver taking a faster corridor in heavy rain was not acting for his own benefit (F10, F1).

There are no in-app chat messages at all, so there is no rider instruction on the record that the driver ignored before leaving the optimal route; nothing in the chat evidence establishes that the rider asked for the shortest route and was overruled (F7).

The only traffic records near the route are speed-band observations (F9, F10, F11) plus the explicit absence of any incident (F12); the driver therefore does not claim a blocked road, only congestion as a reasonable cause for the reroute under RD-4.

This is a RydeTAXI trip (metered, $34.83 total, no surge, waiting $0.00), so any amount computable for the rider must be worked from the per-km rate of $1.4098 derived from this trip's own distance fare (F6, F5, F4).

The driver is an established account (1382 days, 928 trips in 90 days) with 2 upheld disputes, of which none is a route dispute (route: 0), so the rider's complaint does not show a pattern of routing abuse (F15).

weaknesses: The system record flatly contradicts the driver's premise in part: F12 records no traffic incident near the route, so the driver cannot use RD-4(a) (incident-based exemption), and F9's band 2 observation alone is expressly not sufficient to exempt a segment under RD-4(b) in this MVP — the rider will argue the 5.01 km extra is therefore unexcused (F3, F9, F12).

The driver's reroute explanation rests only on his post-trip statement (F8), and RD-4 requires traffic corroboration targeting the replaced portion of the optimal route; the band-2 window (08:49–09:13) ends exactly when the off-route segment begins (09:13), so the rider will say there is no coverage evidence during the segment itself (F3, F8, F9).

There is no chat record of any agreement or even notification to the rider (F7), so if the judge treats the reroute as unexcused the calculable exposure is the excess of $7.53 over 5.34 km billed at $1.4098/km (F4), against which the driver has no consent (RD-5) to point to.

points.response: The AYE band-2 record (F9, 10–19 km/h) runs 08:49–09:13 and therefore expires at the very minute the off-route segment begins (F3, 09:13–09:24), so it does not cover the segment it is offered to excuse; and under RD-4(b) a speed band is corroboration only and does not exempt a segment on its own.

RD-4 requires traffic corroboration aimed at the replaced portion of the optimal route (an incident under (a) or a covering band under (b)) — weather is not listed as a qualifying record, and F12 records no traffic incident near the route during the trip window; heavy rain (F13) explains why a road was slow, it does not excuse 5.01 km of extra distance (F3).

The driver's own account (F8) says he 'went round' the expressway, not that he used the Central Expressway, and no fact ties the driven segment to the CTE or to any named road; a faster corridor elsewhere in the city also fails the RD-4 test because the exemption must target the replaced portion of the optimal route, not a different road's speed (F10).

The absence of chat (F7) is fatal to the driver's side, not the rider's: RD-5 requires the rider's own message agreeing to the route change before the segment starts, and with no messages at all (F7) plus the driver's post-trip explanation (F8) there is neither consent nor even notification, while the driver's RD-1 duty to take the shortest and most direct route is independent of any rider instruction.

Conceding that the driver relies only on congestion, that concession still loses: RD-4(a)'s incident branch is unmet because F12 records no incident, and RD-4(b) expressly will not exempt on a band record alone, so the segment stands unexempted.

We agree the metered rate is $1.4098/km taken from this trip's own fare (F4, total charged $34.83 per F6, no surge per F5), and applying it to the segment's added 5.01 km (F3) yields the $7.06 we request under RD-2.

The driver's profile (F15) shows 3 disputes with 2 upheld in 90 days, so if any account action follows an upheld deviation the profile supports a flag_account as an additional action only; the finding itself rests on the GPS excess in F1 and F3, not on the profile.

We stand on the smaller, clause-permitted figure: RD-2 refunds the unexempted segment's extra km, so $7.06 (5.01 km × $1.4098/km, F3 and F4) is the correct amount and not the wider $7.53 residual of billed excess.

Conceded as to the framework: this is a metered RydeTAXI trip (F6), so the fixed-quote branch does not apply and RD-2's metered formula governs quantum — but that formula only bites once a segment is left unexempted, which is the disputed step.

The distance and duration figures (F1, F2) show a longer trip, not that the deviation was unjustified: RD-1 itself excuses a departure taken 'in the absence of any reasonable cause', and the recorded severe congestion on the corridor's expressways (F9, F10) plus 18.5 mm of thundery rain (F13) supply that cause.

The rider's own concession that the AYE band-2 record shows stop-and-go conditions (F9, 10–19 km/h) undermines 'no exemption applies'; a driver facing an expressway running at 10–19 km/h in a 18.5 mm downpour (F13) had a reasonable cause under RD-4 read with RD-1, and the empty chat (F7) shows no rider instruction was countermanded.

I do not rest on the incident branch: F12's absence of incidents is accepted, but RD-4(a) is one route to 'reasonable cause', not the only one — the driver's reroute basis is congestion, evidenced by F9/F10 bands and the weather in F13, not by a blocked road.

The rider reads RD-4(b) as if band data were the driver's whole case; F9 (AYE, band 2, 08:49–09:13) and F10 (CTE, band 5, 40–49 km/h, 08:49–09:34) together show the corridor was congested end-to-end while a faster parallel expressway existed, and F13 records the heavy rain the driver cites in F8 — corroboration that goes to whether the departure was justified, which is the question RD-1 asks.

The arithmetic is internally inconsistent and premature: the rider takes the per-km rate from F4 ($7.53 ÷ 5.34 km = $1.4098/km) but multiplies the segment's 5.01 km from F3, and RD-2 makes any refund conditional on an unexempted segment, which the traffic and weather facts (F9, F10, F13) rebut.

No refund figure is owed because the segment is exempt on the reasonable-cause ground (F9, F10, F13) — RD-1's 'absence of any reasonable cause' condition is not met, so RD-2's metered formula never engages; the $7.06 versus $7.53 dispute is moot.

RD-6 requires that the case be made out against the driver (RD-2 refund > 0 or a recorded RD-1 breach) before any flag; here there is no upheld breach, and F15 shows the driver's route-dispute count is zero (route: 0) over 90 days, so the flag premise fails.

Agreed that no threat or dangerous-driving allegation appears (F7, F8) so SAFE-1/SAFE-2 do not apply; but that cuts for the driver too — the complaint is a fare dispute only, and on the merits the recorded congestion and rain (F9, F10, F13) support no_action.

Withdrawn to the extent it suggested the AYE band record is a complete answer: I accept RD-4(b) that a band alone does not exempt a segment in this MVP, and my case rests on the cumulative congestion plus weather picture (F9, F10, F13) under RD-1's reasonable-cause standard, not on band 2 alone.
